Hi all — pulling the telemetry/cookie answers together below (feel free to paste into the SQ):

1) Console telemetry (default):
- Session heartbeat: anonymous session pings used for routing/metrics; no PII retained.
- API request metrics: latency, error rates, token counts (per-tenant aggregated, not tied to user identifiers).
- Feature usage: which console pages and buttons are used (page path, tenant id).

2) Docs site cookies:
- _redwood_session: session cookie for docs site (expires at session end).
- _ga, _gid: Google Analytics (anonymized, can be disabled via cookie banner).
- telemetry_opt_out: when present, suppresses non-essential telemetry from the docs site only.

3) Tenant-level controls & opt-out:
- Customers can disable non-essential telemetry at the tenant level via a support request to privacy@redwood.ai; we provide a tenant opt-out flag that suppresses console feature-usage and session-level pings while preserving critical observability for SLA safety.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, telemetry defaults to off, and customers control what (if any) telemetry is sent to Redwood.

4) Evidence / where to look in the docs:
- Console telemetry & cookie matrix: https://redwood.example.com/docs/console/telemetry (also attached CSV).
- Privacy policy excerpt and retention windows are in the SOC 2 packet Neha shared.

If you'd like, I can produce a single-sheet mapping that fits into the SQ (csv + one-paragraph answers).

—Aditya
